earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Rowlands 1962 classificatory notes and Gunn & Conant 1960 ethnography; no phonological description of Basa-Gumna found

sources.note: 'No known L1 speakers. The last fluent speaker shifted to Hausa [hau] by 1987.' Status 10 (Extinct). No resources listed.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, 11 May 2012, 369 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (Wayback copy of rogerblench.info PDF).
sources.note: Sec. 3.4 p. 13: Gumna deserted c. 1963, people at Yakila; 'In Yakila in 1986, there were only two people who spoke Basa, and that not well, so it is effectively dead.' Sec. 4.4 Basa-cluster phonology (p. 32) is an empty placeholder; all Basa-Gumna rows in the comparative wordlist appendix are blank; 'stress' occurs nowhere in the 369 pp.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. c. 2012. The Basa languages (web page, rogerblench.info Kainji/Basa/BasaOP.htm; Wayback copy).
sources.note: Classification list of seven Basa lects; no Basa-Gumna document linked; Wayback CDX of the site shows no Basa-Gumna wordlist was ever posted.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid basa1280 (page, JSON) and reference records 79196, 99051, 66310, 115581, 306337.
sources.note: Only two references for the language, both MED 'wordlist_or_less': Rowlands 1962 (short 'Kuta' word list; lgcode 'Bassa-Kuta from Kagara = [bsl]') and Gunn & Conant 1960 (ethnography). No grammar, sketch or phonology exists in Glottolog.
Cites only Ethnologue, Glottolog, Multitree and Blench 2012; nothing linguistic.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020 [ed. IV, 2019]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 39 Basa-Gumna–Basa-Kontagora cluster.
sources.note: Entry 39 '*Basa-Gumna [†]': alt. names Gwadara-Basa, Basa Kuta, Basa-Kaduna; Niger State, Chanchaga LGA; 'Only 2 known semi-speakers in 1987... Probably now extinct. Source(s) Blench (1987)'; sec. 4.1: 'Basa-Gumna, a Basa lect, no competent speakers in 1987'. No linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In J. R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Table 25 p. 96 lists Basa-Gumna as extinct; p. 96 'for other languages in the cluster only wordlist data exists'; p. 97 'Tones were not marked when this data was collected' (Basa-Benue data). Nothing on stress for any Basa lect.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135.
sources.note: Table 3 p. 99: '(Basa-Gumna)† — Interview with last rememberer (Blench 1976)'; p. 100: Basa-Gumna among Kainji languages that 'have become moribund... without ever being described, let alone documented'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1976/1986. Basa-Gumna: interview with last rememberer / field notes (unpublished; cited as 'Blench 1976' in McGill & Blench 2012 Table 3 and 'Blench (1987)' in the Atlas of Nigerian Languages).
